historical_basis: The Fenixmännlein (also Fenixmännel, Fenskemännel, Fenesleute) are earth sprites and dwarfs of German folklore, once known in Silesia, especially the Oderské vrchy and Hrubý Jeseník, and in the Saxon part of Lusatia. Derivation from the Venedigermännlein ('little Venetian men') is supported since both are bigger than dwarfs but smaller than humans; the Fenixmännlein live collectively in hills and shrubbery. Inside the mountains they hold big parties; they are said to own the original Silesian streuselkuchen recipe, and when they bake in their caves smoke rises from earth holes. A ploughboy who asked for cake was at once handed a cabbage cake with linseed oil by an invisible hand, threatened to eat it on an iron table; he used his ploughshare as that table.
